description: This linear walk climbs to Ben Gullipen in the Loch Lomond and the Trossachs National Park. The hill rises to the south-west of Callander, offering a rewarding vantage point without the demands of a full mountain ascent. The route passes through stretches of woodland and open moorland, with fine views across the surrounding hills and valleys as you gain height. From the summit, there are excellent panoramas towards Ben Ledi, Loch Venachar, and the wider Trossachs landscape. The terrain is a mix of grassy paths and forest tracks, making it a popular option for walkers seeking a moderate and scenic outing. On clear days, the views extend across the Forth Valley and towards the distant HighlandsYou can continue your walking in the area on theLoch Venachar and Loch Drunkie Walk or Cycleand theLoch Rusky Walk.
